subject: Re: BridgeX — uptime backstop, operational asks and approval path
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: BridgeX: ask — short-term uptime backstop and operational asks

Team,

Quick context: BridgeX (large B2B analytics customer) is asking for a one-off commitment as part of a high-touch pilot: 99.95% monthly uptime + a sub-100ms p95 on inference for the US-east region during normal load. They want that in writing for procurement to move forward this week.

What I need from each of you by EOD tomorrow:
- Laura: any redlines we should not accept on credit caps / indemnity.
- Markus: what operational controls we require to meet p95 target and whether we can commit 100ms at pilot scale without a capacity reservation.
- Grace: commercial asks (credits, go-live plan) and whether CS can commit to the runbook and a weekly health sync.

Attaching a quick draft of the SLA language I plan to share with them. I recommend keeping the wording conservative and adding a "backstop" clause: automatic regional fallback to our reserved pool and a capped credit ladder instead of unlimited credits.

Thanks — Jordan

Attachments: bridgex-proposed-sla-draft.pdf

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Chu <ethan.chu@bridgex.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, BridgeX Procurement <procurement@bridgex.io>
Date: 2027-05-19T11:08:00-07:00
Subject: BridgeX SLA draft + operational asks (pilot)

Ethan —

Thanks for taking the time today. Per our call, attaching a short SLA draft and a proposed operational checklist we can follow for the pilot. Highlights:
- Commitment: 99.95% monthly uptime, with a p95 inference latency target of 100ms for US-east during normal pilots.
- Backstop: If p95 slips >20% for two consecutive days, traffic is routed to our reserved pool and BridgeX receives a defined credit ladder (capped at 5% of monthly invoice).
- Monitoring hooks: we add a health webhook and a shared dashboard for the pilot.

Please review the attached SLA and send any redlines. If acceptable, we can send a DocuSign for signature and schedule a technical onboarding with Markus and Grace next week.

Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
jordan.blake@redwood.ai | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: bridgex-proposed-sla-draft.pdf

From: Ethan Chu <ethan.chu@bridgex.io>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: BridgeX Procurement <procurement@bridgex.io>
Date: 2027-05-20T08:24:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeX SLA draft + operational asks (pilot)

Jordan —

Thanks, received and reviewed. High level reaction: BridgeX is comfortable with the uptime backstop structure but we need two adjustments before procurement will sign:
1) p95 target: we asked for 90ms due to strict UX constraints (we can accept staged ramp if you prefer).
2) Volume guarantee: we anticipate bursts up to 3x baseline during marketing events; we need assurance you can scale or provide a temporary uplift without manual approvals.

Attached is a small volume forecast. If you can confirm the 90ms p95 is feasible at pilot load and we can have an agreed escalations path for burst capacity, procurement will move this through next week.

—Ethan

Attachment: bridgex-volumes.xlsx

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-20T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeX SLA draft + operational asks (pilot)

Short answer: 90ms p95 at pilot scale is tight but potentially achievable with conditions.

Key operational constraints and proposed compensating controls:
- Provision a temporary reserved pool (dedicated burst nodes) for BridgeX events; autoscaling alone is risky for guaranteed latency at 90ms.
- Require traffic shaping on client side for marketing spikes OR pre-notify us 48h before planned spikes to pre-warm KV caches and warm routing.
- Add an automatic fallback rule to route noisy tails to a slightly higher-latency cost tier (we'll keep p95 target for 95% of requests and route the rest). This keeps UX good for most users while protecting the platform.
- Monitoring: we'll push a dedicated dashboard and a webhook subscription; team on-call will get immediate paging if p95 > 120ms for >5 minutes.

If legal accepts the capped credit ladder and procurement signs off on a reserved pool uplift fee for burst days, engineering can support the 90ms ask for pilot.

—Markus

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-05-21T09:37:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeX SLA draft + operational asks (pilot)

Jordan / team —

I reviewed the draft and Markus's operational asks. Legal is fine with the backstop model provided we: 
- Retain a maximum credit cap of 5% of monthly charges (do not accept unlimited credits).
- Limit the credit window to the pilot month + 30 days.
- Add a clause that requires BridgeX to provide contemporaneous traffic intent (pre-notification) for planned bursts; without notification we escalate but do not accept blanket liability.

I've attached a redlined version with specific language for the credit ladder, notice requirements, and a mutual force-majeure carve-out for platform-level network outages. Please review and I can produce the DocuSign-ready version once signoffs are in.

Attachment: bridgex-redlines.docx

—Laura

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Ethan Chu <ethan.chu@bridgex.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>, BridgeX Procurement <procurement@bridgex.io>
Date: 2027-05-23T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: BridgeX SLA draft + operational asks (pilot)

Ethan —

Appreciate the quick turn. Summary of alignment and next steps:
- We can accept the 90ms p95 for the pilot provided BridgeX agrees to: a) pre-notify for anticipated bursts (48h), and b) allow temporary reserved pool uplift for event days (uplift fee TBD).
- Legal will cap credits at 5% and limit the credit window to pilot month + 30 days.
- Engineering will publish a shared dashboard and webhook; on-call paging will trigger if p95 >120ms for 5+ minutes.

If that works, Laura will convert the redlines to a DocuSign envelope and I’ll route it to procurement. Also proposing a technical onboarding call Thursday to review the runbook (Markus + Grace + your SRE).

Next: let me know consent and preferred times for the onboarding call and I’ll get the DocuSign out.

Thanks — Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
